summary: Refero's motion guide for product UI says every animation must serve feedback, continuity or hierarchy, or be removed. It orders motion as a pyramid from micro feedback to rare expressive motion, and gives purpose-based duration bands, enter/exit/change easing curves, spring settings, and concrete specs for buttons, inputs, lists, modals and drawers. It defines a minimum and a complete set of motion tokens with a component mapping, and makes a reduced-motion variant mandatory. It ends with anti-patterns (slow hovers, linear easing, transition: all, endless loops) and a pre-ship checklist. For a design system it supplies ready duration, easing, distance and spring token values and the rules for applying them.
key_ideas: Every animation must provide feedback, continuity or hierarchy; otherwise remove it
Decide context first: product UI is subtle and fast, marketing can be more expressive
Higher-frequency and smaller-distance actions get shorter durations
Start with micro feedback; add state transitions, layout continuity and expressive motion only when justified
Use duration bands by purpose rather than one duration for everything
Ease-out for entering, ease-in for exiting, ease-in-out for state changes
Springs suit drag, swipe and physical elements but must settle quickly
Define motion tokens for durations, easings and distances to keep a team consistent
Always ship a prefers-reduced-motion variant: swap slide and scale for fades, remove parallax
Never use transition: all; list the animated properties
Set transform-origin to where the element comes from
Animations must be interruptible by user input
In product UI nothing should exceed 500ms

claims.claim: 500ms or more in product UI almost always feels slow.
claims.evidence: Timing Rules: 500ms+ in product UI almost always feels slow

claims.claim: Linear easing feels robotic and unnatural.
300-600ms on hover or buttons feels sluggish.
transition: all animates unintended properties, causes layout recalculation every frame and hurts performance on low-end devices.
Transforms on SVG elements behave differently and need a wrapping g with transform-box: fill-box.
For most SaaS products CSS plus Motion is sufficient.

quotes: When in doubt — shorter, subtler, or none.
Motion that doesn't serve function is noise.
Spring must decay quickly. No prolonged "jello" effect.

rules.rule: Remove any animation that does not provide feedback, continuity or hierarchy, or whose removal would not hurt the UX.
rules.why: Motion that doesn't serve function is noise.
rules.evidence: Motion serves three purposes; Quick Test

rules.rule: Use 90-150ms for hover, press, toggle and focus; 160-240ms for accordions, tabs and small panels; 240-360ms for modals, drawers and route transitions; 360-500ms only for rare large layout reflows.
rules.why: Purpose-based categories instead of 500ms for everything.

rules.rule: Make smaller-distance and higher-frequency actions shorter; make anything users do 100 times a day instant.
rules.why: Timing rules.

rules.rule: Keep every product UI animation at or under 500ms.
rules.why: 500ms+ almost always feels slow.

rules.rule: Use ease-out for elements entering, ease-in for elements exiting and ease-in-out for state changes, with cubic-bezier(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1), cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.0, 1, 1) and cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1).
rules.why: Enter: fast start, soft landing; exit: soft start, fast exit; change: smooth both ways.

rules.rule: Never use linear easing in product UI.
rules.why: Robotic, unnatural.

rules.rule: Use springs for drag, swipe, gesture responses and physical-feeling elements, and make them settle quickly; snappy is stiffness 400 / damping 30, smooth is stiffness 200 / damping 20.
rules.why: Springs suit physical motion, but a spring that does not settle reads as jello.

rules.rule: Use the bouncy spring (stiffness 300, damping 15) sparingly.
rules.why: Marked use sparingly.

rules.rule: On buttons, shift background color on hover in 120ms, scale to 0.98 on press in 90-120ms, show the focus ring in 120ms, and do not animate the disabled state.
rules.why: Micro-interactions with maximum effect, minimum risk.

rules.rule: Show a clear loading state on buttons, not just a spinner.
rules.why: Listed in Buttons and Controls.

rules.rule: Highlight input focus with border or underline without layout shift; shake on error only on submit, about 200ms, never on every keystroke.
rules.why: Input micro-interaction guidance.

rules.rule: Animate added list rows with a fade plus 4-8px slide over 200ms and removed rows with a fade plus collapse over 180ms; animate reorder only if performant.
rules.why: Lists and Tables guidance.

rules.rule: Fade overlays in over 200ms and out over 150ms; fade and scale modals from 0.95 on enter and to 0.95 on exit; slide drawers from and to their edge.
rules.why: Modals and Drawers table.

rules.rule: Define motion tokens for durations (120ms / 200ms / 320ms), easings and micro-slide distances (4px / 8px / 16px) and use them instead of random values.
rules.why: Prevents chaos across a team.

rules.rule: Map hover/press and tooltips to --duration-fast with --ease-out, accordion/tabs to --duration-default with --ease-in-out, and modal/drawer to --duration-slow with --ease-out entering and --ease-in exiting.
rules.why: Component Mapping table.

rules.rule: Always provide a prefers-reduced-motion variant: replace slide or scale plus fade with fade only, make spring bounce instant or a short tween, remove parallax and pause or remove auto-playing loops.
rules.why: Reduced motion is not optional.

rules.rule: In reduced motion, set fast and default durations to 0ms, slow durations to 100ms and motion distances to 0px.
rules.why: Reference token overrides.

rules.rule: Never use transition: all; list the transitioned properties explicitly.
rules.why: It animates unintended properties, causes layout recalculation and makes debugging hard.

rules.rule: Set transform-origin explicitly for scale and rotate: center for modals and button presses, the trigger corner (top left or top right) for dropdowns, and the edge nearest the trigger for tooltips.
rules.why: The source's common origins place it where the trigger is; scale and rotate need an explicit origin.

rules.rule: To transform SVG parts, wrap them in a g with transform-box: fill-box and transform-origin: center.
rules.why: Transforms on SVG elements behave differently.

rules.rule: Make animations interruptible; avoid fill modes or delays that block interaction.
rules.why: User input should interrupt any animation mid-flight.

rules.rule: Do not run infinite loops in product screens or animate everything at once.
rules.why: Listed as red flags that instantly make motion feel cheap: loops distract, and animating everything at once leaves no attention hierarchy.

rules.rule: Do not use 300-600ms durations on hover or buttons.
rules.why: Feels sluggish.

rules.rule: Use CSS transitions for micro feedback and simple states and Motion for layout animations and springs in React; reach for GSAP, Rive or Lottie only for complex timelines or illustrative motion.
rules.why: For most SaaS products CSS + Motion is sufficient.

rules.rule: Keep timings consistent across similar components; do not use 200ms in one place and 400ms in a similar one.
rules.why: Inconsistent timings are a red flag: chaos.
rules.evidence: Red Flags: Inconsistent timings; Pre-Ship Checklist

rules.rule: Keep product UI motion subtle, fast and functional; allow more expressive motion only on marketing surfaces.
rules.why: Context first: product UI or marketing changes how much motion is acceptable.

rules.rule: Show input success with a subtle checkmark or color change, without overdoing it.
rules.why: Inputs table: Don't overdo it.

rules.rule: Performance-test motion on slower devices before shipping.
rules.why: Pre-ship checklist item; transition: all is a performance killer on low-end devices.

decisions.question: How much motion should the product use?

options.name: Level 1 micro feedback
options.effect: Responsive feel without noticeable animation on hover, press, focus, toggles, inline validation

options.name: Level 2 state transitions
options.effect: Movement instead of teleportation for accordions, tabs, modals, drawers, popovers

options.name: Level 3 layout continuity
options.effect: Elements resize, reorder, add or remove while keeping context
options.when: Reorder, filter chips, drag and drop, lists

decisions.recommendation: Start at Level 1 and add higher levels only when justified; when in doubt, shorter, subtler or none.

decisions.question: Which easing curve for each kind of movement?

options.name: emphasized cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.0, 0, 1)
options.when: Alternative when more character is wanted

decisions.recommendation: Group easings by job: enter, exit, change.

decisions.question: How should springy motion be set up?
decisions.recommendation: Springs for drag, swipe and physical elements, decaying quickly; CSS tweens elsewhere.
decisions.evidence: When to Use Spring; Appendix SPRINGS

decisions.question: How many duration steps should the token set have?
decisions.recommendation: Start with the three-step minimum set.

decisions.question: What should happen when the user asks for reduced motion?

options.name: Fade only
options.effect: Slide or scale plus fade becomes a plain fade

options.name: Remove
options.effect: Parallax gone; auto-playing loops paused or removed

decisions.recommendation: Always provide the variant; the CSS shortcut sets durations to 0.01ms.

process.detail: Product UI or marketing? How often is it triggered? Does it help or distract?
Start with micro feedback; justify each step up.
Match purpose and frequency to a duration category; ease-out to enter, ease-in to exit, ease-in-out to change.
Apply duration, easing and distance tokens through the component mapping.
Fade only, no parallax, paused loops; override tokens under prefers-reduced-motion.
Purpose, frequency-appropriate duration, non-linear easing, reduced-motion variant, would removing it hurt? Remove if no to purpose or removal.
Check bands, tokens, no linear, under 500ms, no transition: all, transform-origin set, interruptible, tested on slower devices.

caveats: Opinionated guide from Refero's design skill; values are presented as defaults, not measured research.
Easing curves are described as Material-inspired; the source does not cite the Material spec version.
Spring presets are Framer Motion / Motion parameters and do not transfer directly to other spring APIs [inferred].
The 0.01ms reduced-motion shortcut removes all motion including fades, which differs from the guide's own fade-only recommendation [inferred].
